name: New Zealand
law: Duty and GST are only collected at the border on parcels worth over NZ$1,000. Below that, the overseas shop charges GST at checkout and nothing is collected at the border, except on alcohol and tobacco. Customs does not phone people about money owed: the courier or freight company collects a real charge.

questions.prompt: Does the caller say a tax, duty or customs charge (such as VAT, GST or import tax) must be paid before a parcel is delivered?

options.text: Yes: a tax, duty or customs charge to pay before delivery

questions.prompt: What is in the parcel, and what is it worth?

options.text: Worth more than 1,000 New Zealand dollars
Worth 1,000 New Zealand dollars or less

questions.prompt: How does the caller ask for the charge to be paid?
questions.hint: The courier's own website means its usual website, found by the person and used with the tracking or reference number from their order. A link or a payment page that the caller sends, or a web address or phone number that the caller reads out to pay with, is the caller's link.

options.text: On the courier's or postal service's own website, or at a post office or on delivery, using the tracking or reference number
By card or bank details given during this call
Through a link, a payment page, or a number that the caller sends or reads out

rules.label: scam
rules.why: New Zealand collects duty and GST at the border only on parcels worth over NZ$1,000. Below that the overseas shop charges GST at checkout and nothing is collected at the border, so this tax doesn't exist and the payment page is a trap.
rules.advice: Don't pay. Track the parcel on the courier's own website, typed in yourself.

rules.label: scam
rules.why: New Zealand Customs does not phone people about money owed, and a real charge on a parcel is collected by the courier or freight company, not by card or bank details given on a call.
rules.advice: Don't pay through anything the caller gives you. Find the courier's website yourself and pay there with your tracking number, or at a post office.

rules.label: legit
rules.why: New Zealand collects duty and GST at the border on parcels worth over NZ$1,000, and on alcohol and tobacco whatever their value, so a charge before delivery is expected.

rules.label: unsure
rules.why: A charge before delivery can be real for this parcel, but the call doesn't say how to pay it, or the caller gives the link or number to pay with.
rules.advice: Don't pay through anything the caller gives you. Find the courier's website yourself and pay there with your tracking number, or at a post office.

rules.label: unsure
rules.why: In New Zealand a charge at the border is real only on parcels worth over NZ$1,000, or on alcohol and tobacco, and the call doesn't say what this parcel is or what it's worth.
rules.advice: Check what you paid for it: at NZ$1,000 or less, nothing is due at the border.
